legacy_audit.reason_non_actionable: This legacy calculation treated a present value as a future payoff and cannot be used as a forward return, hurdle entry price, ranking signal, or capital decision.

low.label: subsequent_consumption
low.rationale: October repurchases consumed USD 648 million. Retain an additional allowance for net subsequent movements without crediting unknown receipts; separately fund November obligations.

low.label: g1
low.rationale: Desired installed-business nominal growth is -10%, 11% and 14%, before the separate forward acquisition contribution and subject to executable internal funding. Aggregate net revenue grew 12.23% in 2024 and 16.42% in 2025. Current nine-month currency-neutral network growth of 9% and services growth of 18%, weighted by their approximately 59%/41% revenue mix, imply about 12.7%. Base discounts this measured mix for slower activity and renewal concessions; high permits durable services distribution. Low combines spending contraction, weaker cross-border mix and program losses.

low.label: g2
low.rationale: Desired installed growth remains near the measured recent network/services mix in base and high, with actual growth limited by internally available capital. The low recovery remains incomplete after the initial contraction. Recent aggregate revenue growth of 12.23% and 16.42% supports persistence; incentives growing faster than net network revenue warrant moderation rather than extrapolating gross assessments.

low.label: g3
low.rationale: Desired installed growth of 10% and 13% retains adoption and shared services distribution close to the current approximately 12.7% currency-neutral mix. The downside recovers slowly with lasting margin concessions. Annual funding limits can reduce achieved growth while preserving maintenance, renewal expense, contractual payments and operating liquidity.

low.label: runway_growth
low.rationale: Start subsequent desired installed growth at 2%, 10% and 13%. Base and high retain substantial adoption/services persistence relative to 2024–2025 aggregate net revenue growth of 12.23%–16.42% and the current approximately 12.7% currency-neutral network/services mix. Long customer contracts, shared acceptance and distribution support opportunity, while variable consideration guarantees neither volumes nor renewal economics. Actual growth remains subject to each year's funded deployment ceiling.

low.label: fade
low.rationale: Reduce desired installed growth by two percentage points annually in low, 0.6 points in base and 0.4 points in high, subject to the mature-growth floor. Base reaches mature growth around explicit year 18; high still grows approximately 4.6% in year 25. This materially distinguishes rapid erosion from durable distribution. Competitive mechanisms are issuer concessions, local routing, account-based substitutes and services-market saturation; the funding horizon does not establish the fade.

low.label: mature_growth
low.rationale: After elevated growth fades, nominal installed-business growth is modest. Prices, payment amounts, wages, replacement costs and customer funding remain linked; no separate inflation uplift is added.

low.label: terminal_growth
low.rationale: Continuation after the last existing debt maturity grows no faster than mature economics. Downside mature owner earnings are flat at realization despite modest preceding recovery. Growth requires funded incremental equity.

low.label: prefinance_margin
low.rationale: After-tax accounting earnings margin before existing debt interest, with ordinary litigation, depreciation and SBC still charged. Reconciled trailing income plus after-tax interest is about 48.8% of revenue. Base discounts tax benefits and grants; downside imposes lasting concessions and operating deleverage.

low.label: trailing_interest
low.rationale: Reconstruct trailing reported interest expense from USD 722 million annual expense plus USD 653 million current nine-month expense less USD 563 million comparative expense. Use this solely to reconcile the reported baseline before forecasting retiring debt separately.

low.label: tax_rate
low.rationale: Use a normalized marginal tax rate for interest adjustments, above recent effective rates affected by discrete benefits. Ordinary operating taxes remain in the earnings margin.

low.label: cash_recast
low.rationale: Retain a numerical recast of USD 1,241 million: trailing prepaid outflows 5,137 less incentive amortization 2,602 less accrued-expense inflows 2,838 less customer-deposit inflows 193 plus net settlement outflows 23 plus litigation-liability outflows 675 plus receivable outflows 1,039, all in USD millions. This recasts identified timing and capital movements before separately funding incremental customer capital; ordinary incentive amortization, renewal economics and legal expense remain in reported net earnings. Mixed classifications justify the -1,500 to +2,000 million bounds, jointly tested with conversion and customer funding.

low.label: conversion_persistence
low.rationale: Retain 92%, 98% and 102% persistence of numerically reconstructed prefinancing conversion. Current nine-month OCF fell while net income rose, whereas the 2023–2025 cash proxy after physical/software spending, SBC and customer-deposit inflows improved materially. These competing observations support bounded conversion rather than treating all weak cash as deterioration or all incentive payments as investment. The renewal stress now reduces achieved organic growth when the joint capital requirement exceeds internal resources.

low.label: maintenance_ratio
low.rationale: Trailing physical purchases and software capitalization total about USD 1,431 million. Revenue-linked replacement and resilience spending is embedded in owner earnings; expansion software and equipment belong to separately funded organic deployment. Expensed development remains charged.

low.label: sbc_factor
low.rationale: Embed economic compensation funding above trailing SBC intensity once. Reported cash conversion adds back noncash SBC; the funding deduction supports cash-equivalent compensation or funded participation neutralization. Constant shares receive no repurchase benefit.

low.label: owner_translation
low.rationale: Translate the reported USD 2,094 million annual net-income increment into a bounded maintenance-adjusted owner-earnings proxy. Annual physical and software spending was USD 1,215 million against USD 1,143 million depreciation and amortization in 2025; accounting earnings are an approximate incremental numerator, not measured marginal cash returns.

low.label: organic_attribution
low.rationale: Attribute 40%, 55% and 70% of the nonacquired owner-earnings increment to newly funded organic capital; the remainder reflects installed-network activity, pricing, operating leverage and older investments. After the corrected acquisition contribution, attributed organic earnings are approximately USD 728 million, USD 1,098 million and USD 1,521 million. Apply the identical attribution to forward incremental earnings before dividing by the calibrated return. Customer funding and incremental operating liquidity remain independent floors.

low.label: organic_calibration_capital
low.rationale: During 2025, incentive assets increased USD 1,997 million and receivables USD 836 million. The USD 4,400 million, USD 3,700 million and USD 3,400 million capital estimates also allow expansion and operating-liquidity deployment, excluding acquisitions and maintenance already charged. With corrected acquisition attribution, incremental organic returns are approximately 16.6%, 29.7% and 44.7%. These are uncertain earnings/capital estimates with investment lags, not book ROE. Forward funding applies the same attributed-profit boundary; complete continuation returns include installed gains and all funded capital.

low.label: acquisition_budget
low.rationale: Retain USD 1,300 million of annual prospective acquisitions against USD 2,511 million spent in 2024, none in 2025 and USD 1,372 million in the latest nine months. Purchases remain fully charged even when payback fails. Their estimated payoff is now calibrated to disclosed acquired revenue and a bounded owner margin, producing returns below the equity hurdle rather than assuming purchased compounding. Organic expansion is rationed before contractual funding, the acquisition budget or already embedded maintenance is compromised.

low.label: acquisition_payoff
low.rationale: Forward purchases earn the revised acquired-revenue-based return after a one-year integration delay. A zero-payoff test preserves all purchases and BVNK contingent consideration while removing acquired revenue and owner earnings. This fixed one-year lag is a judgment to monitor, not proof of achieved cohort returns; margins include ordinary integration costs and no synergy uplift.

low.label: customer_intensity
low.rationale: Latest incentive assets increased USD 1,223 million and receivables USD 649 million against comparable nine-month revenue growth of USD 3,497 million. Fund customer capital against positive installed growth and acquired revenue. This floors organic deployment; contraction releases no existing assets.

low.label: bvnk_contingency
low.rationale: Fund the full disclosed possible contingent consideration in year 1 without separate synergy proceeds. This bound applies only to that consideration.

low.label: outside_claims
low.rationale: Embed a recurring cash allowance above reported annual and recent nine-month other-financing outflows for nonparent and residual claims. Ordinary taxes, leases and sponsorship expense remain charged and are not deducted again.

low.label: legal_cash
low.rationale: Additional cash is separate from ordinary legal expense. Block and Intuit seek aggregate single damages above USD 5 billion, alongside European and UK matters. Downside combines adverse outcomes and accelerated collection. Immediate collection is a stress timing judgment; no tax or indemnity recovery is credited.

low.label: settlement_severity
low.rationale: Apply immediate net cash severity to post-mitigation exposure. Downside correlates customer failures with operating weakness. Annual receipts cannot fund a demand due within days.

low.label: facility_access
low.rationale: Timely access rests on the undrawn commitment, permitted settlement-failure use, covenant compliance and November 2030 expiry. Access is discrete; lender performance, representations or default conditions can prevent timely drawing. Commercial paper adds no separate capacity.

low.label: facility_cost
low.rationale: After-tax emergency funding costs exceed ordinary fixed-note costs because facility margins depend on ratings and prevailing rates. Charge a full year on opening drawings before repayment.

low.label: arrears_cost
low.rationale: Charge an additional cash financing and enforcement allowance on early unpaid demands until their modeled year-1 payment. This is a stress cost estimate, not an asserted contractual penalty or legal cap. Existing common owners receive nothing after the early failure.

low.label: liquidity_ratio
low.rationale: The operating minimum is half the latest unrestricted cash, rising with achieved revenue and never automatically declining with contraction. A separate payout and growth-allocation target adds the following year's entire scheduled principal. That full-year prefunding target is discretionary; it is neither an additional current debt payment nor the operating minimum. For the initial intermediate squeeze, an explicit dated minimum additionally reserves December–February principal without receipt credit and March/June cumulative principal net of bounded internal receipts. Preserve every actual maturity payment, acquisition charge and financing cost. Discretionary deployment follows creditor payments and operating liquidity; distributions remain residual.

low.label: coupon_proxy
low.rationale: Approximate cash coupon cost on outstanding principal, informed by the disclosed note coupons, limited floating exposure and the latest interest burden. Unlike perpetual embedded interest, this charge falls with contractual principal retirement. A joint test raises the coupon proxy and removes the tax shield.

low.label: retirement_weight
low.rationale: Approximate within-year interest using average principal: opening principal less the declared fraction of that year's retirement. The maturity table places most payments between winter and summer. This timing estimate affects annual interest only; all principal is paid in its contractual holding year and terminal interest is zero.

low.label: euro_factor
low.rationale: Translate future euro principal relative to the latest reported USD amounts. Downside combines dollar weakness with operating stress. Reconcile the same translation into projected outstanding principal and all affected repayments; it creates no current cash.

low.label: november_principal
low.rationale: Reserve the disclosed November 2026 note before prospective annual receipts; later notes remain outstanding until their own maturity years.

low.label: old_coupon_allowance
low.rationale: Fund a separate early allowance for accrued coupon and cash-timing obligations around the November retirement. The retiring note's annual coupon is USD 22.125 million; the allowance avoids treating pre-holding accruals as free cash. It is not recurring owner expense.

low.label: m1
low.rationale: March 2027 USD principal falls in holding year 1, after the separately reserved November note.

low.label: m2_usd
low.rationale: Year 2 includes the disclosed January, February, March and June 2028 USD maturities. The December 2027 euro note is added separately.

low.label: m2_euro
low.rationale: Latest USD translation of the December 2027 euro note; future payment uses the declared euro factor.

low.label: m3_usd
low.rationale: Year 3 includes the June 2029 USD notes; the February 2029 euro note is separate.

low.label: m3_euro
low.rationale: Latest USD translation of the February 2029 euro note; future payment uses the same euro factor as projected debt.

low.label: m4
low.rationale: March 2030 USD principal is paid in year 4; the December 2030 note belongs to year 5.

low.label: m5_usd
low.rationale: Year 5 pays the March and June 2031 USD notes; the December 2030 euro note is added separately.

low.label: m5_euro
low.rationale: Latest USD translation of the December 2030 euro note; future payment uses the declared euro factor.

low.label: m6
low.rationale: Year 6 pays November 2031 principal and the January and March 2032 USD notes.

low.label: m7
low.rationale: March 2033 principal is paid in year 7.

low.label: m8
low.rationale: May 2034 principal is paid in year 8.

low.label: m9
low.rationale: January 2035 principal is paid in year 9.

low.label: m10
low.rationale: June 2036 principal is paid in year 10. No existing principal matures during holding years 11 through 20.

low.label: m21
low.rationale: November 2046 principal belongs to holding year 21, not year 20.

low.label: m22
low.rationale: February 2048 principal is paid in year 22.

low.label: m23
low.rationale: June 2049 principal is paid in year 23.

low.label: m24
low.rationale: March 2050 principal is paid in year 24.

low.label: m25
low.rationale: March 2051 is the final disclosed existing principal maturity. Retirement precedes terminal realization and eliminates the remaining ordinary debt interest.

low.label: equity_hurdle
low.rationale: Declared nominal USD owner hurdle balances diversified profitable transactions against concentrated customers, incentive funding, intervention and short-duration guarantees. It is a business-specific judgment, not a market-derived default. Keep the rate constant across scenarios because operating deterioration and funding failure are executed in cash flows.

low.label: acquired_revenue_contribution
low.rationale: The 2025 annual revenue bridge attributes approximately three percentage points of services growth to acquisitions. Applied to USD 10,832 million of 2024 services revenue, this gives USD 324.96 million of acquired revenue contribution. The bounds recognize rounding and classification uncertainty, not undisclosed synergies.

low.label: acquired_owner_margin
low.rationale: Convert acquired revenue into incremental after-tax parent owner earnings after ordinary integration costs, maintenance and compensation. This estimates USD 64.992 million, USD 97.488 million and USD 129.984 million against the complete USD 2,511 million purchase-capital denominator: approximately 2.59%, 3.88% and 5.18%. No unquantified parent synergies, margin above acquired revenue, or integration-cost addback is credited. Full purchase consideration remains the equity-capital denominator; forward acquisitions receive no additional borrowing.

low.label: fiscal_first_weight
low.rationale: The January–December 2027 commitment combines January–October from holding year 1 with November–December from holding year 2. Allocate annual operating revenue and recurring cash evenly within each holding year, giving ten-twelfths and two-twelfths. This is an explicit interpolation judgment, not a claim that holding-year and fiscal-year totals are identical. The range tests seasonality and within-year acquisition integration timing.

low.label: m2_pre_march_usd
low.rationale: Aggregate the disclosed January 2028 USD 750 million and February 2028 USD 500 million maturities. December 2027 euro principal remains separately translated through m2_fx. This disaggregation changes neither total principal nor its annual payment.

low.label: m2_march_usd
low.rationale: Aggregate the disclosed March 2028 USD notes: 300 million floating, 450 million fixed and 750 million fixed. The remaining USD 1,750 million matures in June. Preserve the existing annual USD 4,500 million payment.

low.label: march_net_receipts_fraction
low.rationale: By the March 2028 payments, require cumulative net internal cash from November 2027 to equal at least 10% of the conservative year-2 cash envelope. Assume cumulative net cash before March is nonnegative; reserve all December, January and February principal without crediting receipts. The envelope excludes profits from proposed organic expansion and deducts full desired organic funding, acquisitions, acquired-customer capital, incremental acquired operating liquidity, outside claims, note interest and a full opening-draw financing allowance. Weekly customer billing and ordinarily short payment terms support periodic collection. Historical January–March OCF represented approximately 16.0%, 11.3% and 13.5% of annual OCF in 2023–2025. Those observations support a deliberately lower 7.5% stress bound over this longer collection window, but do not establish future net receipt timing.

low.label: june_net_receipts_fraction
low.rationale: By June 2028 require at least 40% of the same conservative annual net cash envelope to have accumulated over November–June. This allows substantial receipt backloading relative to the elapsed eight months. The company bills customers periodically and generated positive first-half OCF in every displayed recent year. Deduct full desired annual deployment and fixed modeled cash uses in the envelope before applying the fraction; do not credit additional borrowing or positive-growth earnings. Stress the fraction jointly with unavailable credit and the intermediate operating squeeze.

base.rationale: Apply immediate net cash severity to post-mitigation exposure. Downside correlates customer failures with operating weakness. Annual receipts cannot fund a demand due within days.

base.label: facility_access
base.rationale: Timely access rests on the undrawn commitment, permitted settlement-failure use, covenant compliance and November 2030 expiry. Access is discrete; lender performance, representations or default conditions can prevent timely drawing. Commercial paper adds no separate capacity.

base.label: facility_cost
base.rationale: After-tax emergency funding costs exceed ordinary fixed-note costs because facility margins depend on ratings and prevailing rates. Charge a full year on opening drawings before repayment.

base.label: arrears_cost
base.rationale: Charge an additional cash financing and enforcement allowance on early unpaid demands until their modeled year-1 payment. This is a stress cost estimate, not an asserted contractual penalty or legal cap. Existing common owners receive nothing after the early failure.

base.label: liquidity_ratio
base.rationale: The operating minimum is half the latest unrestricted cash, rising with achieved revenue and never automatically declining with contraction. A separate payout and growth-allocation target adds the following year's entire scheduled principal. That full-year prefunding target is discretionary; it is neither an additional current debt payment nor the operating minimum. For the initial intermediate squeeze, an explicit dated minimum additionally reserves December–February principal without receipt credit and March/June cumulative principal net of bounded internal receipts. Preserve every actual maturity payment, acquisition charge and financing cost. Discretionary deployment follows creditor payments and operating liquidity; distributions remain residual.

base.label: coupon_proxy
base.rationale: Approximate cash coupon cost on outstanding principal, informed by the disclosed note coupons, limited floating exposure and the latest interest burden. Unlike perpetual embedded interest, this charge falls with contractual principal retirement. A joint test raises the coupon proxy and removes the tax shield.

base.label: retirement_weight
base.rationale: Approximate within-year interest using average principal: opening principal less the declared fraction of that year's retirement. The maturity table places most payments between winter and summer. This timing estimate affects annual interest only; all principal is paid in its contractual holding year and terminal interest is zero.

base.label: euro_factor
base.rationale: Translate future euro principal relative to the latest reported USD amounts. Downside combines dollar weakness with operating stress. Reconcile the same translation into projected outstanding principal and all affected repayments; it creates no current cash.

base.label: november_principal
base.rationale: Reserve the disclosed November 2026 note before prospective annual receipts; later notes remain outstanding until their own maturity years.

base.label: old_coupon_allowance
base.rationale: Fund a separate early allowance for accrued coupon and cash-timing obligations around the November retirement. The retiring note's annual coupon is USD 22.125 million; the allowance avoids treating pre-holding accruals as free cash. It is not recurring owner expense.

base.label: m2_usd

base.label: equity_hurdle
base.rationale: Declared nominal USD owner hurdle balances diversified profitable transactions against concentrated customers, incentive funding, intervention and short-duration guarantees. It is a business-specific judgment, not a market-derived default. Keep the rate constant across scenarios because operating deterioration and funding failure are executed in cash flows.

base.label: acquired_revenue_contribution
base.rationale: The 2025 annual revenue bridge attributes approximately three percentage points of services growth to acquisitions. Applied to USD 10,832 million of 2024 services revenue, this gives USD 324.96 million of acquired revenue contribution. The bounds recognize rounding and classification uncertainty, not undisclosed synergies.

base.label: acquired_owner_margin
base.rationale: Convert acquired revenue into incremental after-tax parent owner earnings after ordinary integration costs, maintenance and compensation. This estimates USD 64.992 million, USD 97.488 million and USD 129.984 million against the complete USD 2,511 million purchase-capital denominator: approximately 2.59%, 3.88% and 5.18%. No unquantified parent synergies, margin above acquired revenue, or integration-cost addback is credited. Full purchase consideration remains the equity-capital denominator; forward acquisitions receive no additional borrowing.

base.label: fiscal_first_weight
base.rationale: The January–December 2027 commitment combines January–October from holding year 1 with November–December from holding year 2. Allocate annual operating revenue and recurring cash evenly within each holding year, giving ten-twelfths and two-twelfths. This is an explicit interpolation judgment, not a claim that holding-year and fiscal-year totals are identical. The range tests seasonality and within-year acquisition integration timing.

base.label: m2_pre_march_usd
base.rationale: Aggregate the disclosed January 2028 USD 750 million and February 2028 USD 500 million maturities. December 2027 euro principal remains separately translated through m2_fx. This disaggregation changes neither total principal nor its annual payment.

base.label: m2_march_usd
base.rationale: Aggregate the disclosed March 2028 USD notes: 300 million floating, 450 million fixed and 750 million fixed. The remaining USD 1,750 million matures in June. Preserve the existing annual USD 4,500 million payment.

base.label: march_net_receipts_fraction
base.rationale: By the March 2028 payments, require cumulative net internal cash from November 2027 to equal at least 10% of the conservative year-2 cash envelope. Assume cumulative net cash before March is nonnegative; reserve all December, January and February principal without crediting receipts. The envelope excludes profits from proposed organic expansion and deducts full desired organic funding, acquisitions, acquired-customer capital, incremental acquired operating liquidity, outside claims, note interest and a full opening-draw financing allowance. Weekly customer billing and ordinarily short payment terms support periodic collection. Historical January–March OCF represented approximately 16.0%, 11.3% and 13.5% of annual OCF in 2023–2025. Those observations support a deliberately lower 7.5% stress bound over this longer collection window, but do not establish future net receipt timing.

base.label: june_net_receipts_fraction
base.rationale: By June 2028 require at least 40% of the same conservative annual net cash envelope to have accumulated over November–June. This allows substantial receipt backloading relative to the elapsed eight months. The company bills customers periodically and generated positive first-half OCF in every displayed recent year. Deduct full desired annual deployment and fixed modeled cash uses in the envelope before applying the fraction; do not credit additional borrowing or positive-growth earnings. Stress the fraction jointly with unavailable credit and the intermediate operating squeeze.

high.label: subsequent_consumption
high.rationale: October repurchases consumed USD 648 million. Retain an additional allowance for net subsequent movements without crediting unknown receipts; separately fund November obligations.

high.label: g1
high.rationale: Desired installed-business nominal growth is -10%, 11% and 14%, before the separate forward acquisition contribution and subject to executable internal funding. Aggregate net revenue grew 12.23% in 2024 and 16.42% in 2025. Current nine-month currency-neutral network growth of 9% and services growth of 18%, weighted by their approximately 59%/41% revenue mix, imply about 12.7%. Base discounts this measured mix for slower activity and renewal concessions; high permits durable services distribution. Low combines spending contraction, weaker cross-border mix and program losses.

high.label: g2
high.rationale: Desired installed growth remains near the measured recent network/services mix in base and high, with actual growth limited by internally available capital. The low recovery remains incomplete after the initial contraction. Recent aggregate revenue growth of 12.23% and 16.42% supports persistence; incentives growing faster than net network revenue warrant moderation rather than extrapolating gross assessments.

high.label: g3
high.rationale: Desired installed growth of 10% and 13% retains adoption and shared services distribution close to the current approximately 12.7% currency-neutral mix. The downside recovers slowly with lasting margin concessions. Annual funding limits can reduce achieved growth while preserving maintenance, renewal expense, contractual payments and operating liquidity.

high.label: runway_growth
high.rationale: Start subsequent desired installed growth at 2%, 10% and 13%. Base and high retain substantial adoption/services persistence relative to 2024–2025 aggregate net revenue growth of 12.23%–16.42% and the current approximately 12.7% currency-neutral network/services mix. Long customer contracts, shared acceptance and distribution support opportunity, while variable consideration guarantees neither volumes nor renewal economics. Actual growth remains subject to each year's funded deployment ceiling.

high.label: fade
high.rationale: Reduce desired installed growth by two percentage points annually in low, 0.6 points in base and 0.4 points in high, subject to the mature-growth floor. Base reaches mature growth around explicit year 18; high still grows approximately 4.6% in year 25. This materially distinguishes rapid erosion from durable distribution. Competitive mechanisms are issuer concessions, local routing, account-based substitutes and services-market saturation; the funding horizon does not establish the fade.

high.label: mature_growth
high.rationale: After elevated growth fades, nominal installed-business growth is modest. Prices, payment amounts, wages, replacement costs and customer funding remain linked; no separate inflation uplift is added.

high.label: terminal_growth
high.rationale: Continuation after the last existing debt maturity grows no faster than mature economics. Downside mature owner earnings are flat at realization despite modest preceding recovery. Growth requires funded incremental equity.

high.label: prefinance_margin
high.rationale: After-tax accounting earnings margin before existing debt interest, with ordinary litigation, depreciation and SBC still charged. Reconciled trailing income plus after-tax interest is about 48.8% of revenue. Base discounts tax benefits and grants; downside imposes lasting concessions and operating deleverage.

high.label: trailing_interest
high.rationale: Reconstruct trailing reported interest expense from USD 722 million annual expense plus USD 653 million current nine-month expense less USD 563 million comparative expense. Use this solely to reconcile the reported baseline before forecasting retiring debt separately.

high.label: tax_rate
high.rationale: Use a normalized marginal tax rate for interest adjustments, above recent effective rates affected by discrete benefits. Ordinary operating taxes remain in the earnings margin.

high.label: cash_recast
high.rationale: Retain a numerical recast of USD 1,241 million: trailing prepaid outflows 5,137 less incentive amortization 2,602 less accrued-expense inflows 2,838 less customer-deposit inflows 193 plus net settlement outflows 23 plus litigation-liability outflows 675 plus receivable outflows 1,039, all in USD millions. This recasts identified timing and capital movements before separately funding incremental customer capital; ordinary incentive amortization, renewal economics and legal expense remain in reported net earnings. Mixed classifications justify the -1,500 to +2,000 million bounds, jointly tested with conversion and customer funding.

high.label: conversion_persistence
high.rationale: Retain 92%, 98% and 102% persistence of numerically reconstructed prefinancing conversion. Current nine-month OCF fell while net income rose, whereas the 2023–2025 cash proxy after physical/software spending, SBC and customer-deposit inflows improved materially. These competing observations support bounded conversion rather than treating all weak cash as deterioration or all incentive payments as investment. The renewal stress now reduces achieved organic growth when the joint capital requirement exceeds internal resources.

high.label: maintenance_ratio
high.rationale: Trailing physical purchases and software capitalization total about USD 1,431 million. Revenue-linked replacement and resilience spending is embedded in owner earnings; expansion software and equipment belong to separately funded organic deployment. Expensed development remains charged.

high.label: sbc_factor
high.rationale: Embed economic compensation funding above trailing SBC intensity once. Reported cash conversion adds back noncash SBC; the funding deduction supports cash-equivalent compensation or funded participation neutralization. Constant shares receive no repurchase benefit.

high.label: owner_translation
high.rationale: Translate the reported USD 2,094 million annual net-income increment into a bounded maintenance-adjusted owner-earnings proxy. Annual physical and software spending was USD 1,215 million against USD 1,143 million depreciation and amortization in 2025; accounting earnings are an approximate incremental numerator, not measured marginal cash returns.

high.label: organic_attribution
high.rationale: Attribute 40%, 55% and 70% of the nonacquired owner-earnings increment to newly funded organic capital; the remainder reflects installed-network activity, pricing, operating leverage and older investments. After the corrected acquisition contribution, attributed organic earnings are approximately USD 728 million, USD 1,098 million and USD 1,521 million. Apply the identical attribution to forward incremental earnings before dividing by the calibrated return. Customer funding and incremental operating liquidity remain independent floors.

high.label: organic_calibration_capital
high.rationale: During 2025, incentive assets increased USD 1,997 million and receivables USD 836 million. The USD 4,400 million, USD 3,700 million and USD 3,400 million capital estimates also allow expansion and operating-liquidity deployment, excluding acquisitions and maintenance already charged. With corrected acquisition attribution, incremental organic returns are approximately 16.6%, 29.7% and 44.7%. These are uncertain earnings/capital estimates with investment lags, not book ROE. Forward funding applies the same attributed-profit boundary; complete continuation returns include installed gains and all funded capital.

high.label: acquisition_budget
high.rationale: Retain USD 1,300 million of annual prospective acquisitions against USD 2,511 million spent in 2024, none in 2025 and USD 1,372 million in the latest nine months. Purchases remain fully charged even when payback fails. Their estimated payoff is now calibrated to disclosed acquired revenue and a bounded owner margin, producing returns below the equity hurdle rather than assuming purchased compounding. Organic expansion is rationed before contractual funding, the acquisition budget or already embedded maintenance is compromised.

high.label: acquisition_payoff
high.rationale: Forward purchases earn the revised acquired-revenue-based return after a one-year integration delay. A zero-payoff test preserves all purchases and BVNK contingent consideration while removing acquired revenue and owner earnings. This fixed one-year lag is a judgment to monitor, not proof of achieved cohort returns; margins include ordinary integration costs and no synergy uplift.

high.label: customer_intensity

high.label: bvnk_contingency

high.label: outside_claims

method_route.decision_rule: Use one primary method and no more than two corroborating methods; irrelevant methods and personas remain silent.

valuation.margin_of_safety_definition: (intrinsic_value_today - market_price) / intrinsic_value_today; positive means the quote is below intrinsic value
valuation.interpretation: output_basis states what the proof produced. value_per_share and present_value_today_per_share are intrinsic values today and are withheld while any material additive component is unpriced or dated future economics cannot be discounted at an explicit required return. priced_components_per_share is the raw proof-output sum. A present value is never annualized or discounted again.

scenario_contract.rule: Cases must change cited causal operating, capital, probability, timing, or financing drivers—not only a terminal multiple.

blockers: Market price per share is missing or non-positive; cannot mark decision_grade or compare value with price.
forward return is not uniquely computable for every scenario from the supplied dated economics
forward_cashflow_schedule output_basis requires required_return_pct to derive intrinsic value today
forward_cashflow_schedule requires low/base/high per-share cash-flow arrays

required_refresh_triggers: new filing or material operating update

change_control.rule: A source fact is locked. Every assumption change requires a reason, author, timestamp, and before/after value.

decision_rule: Proof status and investment readiness are separate. Every material claim must be valued exactly once by a valid calculation proof, every evidence blocker must be resolved, and the model must be stock-specific before committee review. Only a human decision can authorize capital.

shared_forecast.settlement_policy: Explicit cash/debt additions in an operating DCF are time-zero acquisition adjustments; hypothetical settlement, not declared dividends.
